terms.plainEnglish: Shows what changed and what Git is ready to commit.
terms.beginnerExplanation: git status shows what changed without changing anything.
terms.learningExplanation: git status reports working tree and staging area state.
terms.advancedExplanation: git status summarizes index, working tree, branch, and upstream state.
terms.confusion: It only reports information. It does not change files.

terms.plainEnglish: Stages changed files in the current folder for the next commit.
terms.beginnerExplanation: git add . puts your current folder's changes into the next commit.
terms.learningExplanation: git add . stages changes under the current directory in Git's index.
terms.advancedExplanation: git add . updates the index with tracked and untracked path changes under cwd.
terms.confusion: It can stage more than you intended, so check git status first.

terms.plainEnglish: Saves staged changes into Git history with a short message.
terms.beginnerExplanation: git commit -m saves the staged changes with a short note.
terms.learningExplanation: git commit creates a snapshot from staged changes and records the message after -m.
terms.advancedExplanation: git commit writes a new commit object from the current index state.
terms.confusion: It only commits staged changes, not every edited file automatically.

terms.plainEnglish: Uploads your local commits to the connected remote repository.
terms.beginnerExplanation: git push uploads your commits to GitHub or another remote.
terms.learningExplanation: git push sends local commits from your branch to its remote branch.
terms.advancedExplanation: git push updates refs on the remote with local commit objects.
terms.confusion: Push sends commits, not unsaved file changes.

terms.plainEnglish: Downloads remote commits and applies them to your current branch.
terms.beginnerExplanation: git pull brings down new commits from the remote and applies them locally.
terms.learningExplanation: git pull fetches remote changes and merges or rebases them into the current branch.
terms.advancedExplanation: git pull is fetch plus an integration step, depending on configuration.
terms.confusion: Pulling with local edits can create conflicts.

terms.plainEnglish: A separate line of work in Git.
terms.beginnerExplanation: A branch lets you work on changes separately from the main line.
terms.learningExplanation: A branch is a movable name pointing to a commit history line.
terms.advancedExplanation: A branch is a ref that advances as commits are added.
terms.confusion: Switching branches changes which files Git shows in your working folder.

parts.explanation: Means the current folder and everything inside it.

parts.explanation: Sends your commits from your computer to the remote.
